# Expert faceplate
Press [bold]VIEW[/bold] at the top of the radio panel until it reads [bold]117G PANEL[/bold].
The expert faceplate controls the same radio as the [textlink="guided panel" link="AU14CommsANPRCGuided"], but exposes settings and functions that the guided interface normally leaves on AUTO.
Most functions are controlled through the display, keypad, soft keys, and function switch.
## Working the display
Each screen contains a list of settings, actions, and information.
Move the cursor to a usable line, then activate it.
[bold]Control[/bold] [bold]Function[/bold]
[bold]+ PRE / - PRE[/bold] Move the cursor up or down.
[bold]ENT[/bold] Use the selected setting, action, or page.
[bold]CLR[/bold] Return to the previous screen. While typing, delete one character.
[bold]+ PG / - PG[/bold] Move between main pages.
Soft keys Open PGM, SEC, SRCH, LOG, OPT, or the ? key card.
Bright lines can be selected.
Dim lines provide information and are skipped by the cursor.
A lit setting is currently enabled.
### Confirming destructive actions
Some actions require confirmation, including:
- ZEROIZE - DESTROY - RECRYPTO - SEND KEY OTA
Press [bold]ENT[/bold] once to arm the action, then press it again to confirm.
Armed actions cancel automatically after a short delay.
## Keypad
When the radio is not accepting text or numbers, the number keys act as shortcuts.
[bold]Key[/bold] [bold]Function[/bold]
1 CALL Send a radio check on the working net.
2 LT Cycle the display backlight.
3 MODE Cycle the waveform.
4 SQL Cycle squelch.
5 ZERO Open SEC with ZEROIZE armed.
6 PWR Switch the radio on or off.
7 Open OPT.
8 Open PGM.
9 Open SEC.
0 Open LOG.
### Entering values
Some settings require direct input, including:
- frequencies - memory labels - station callsigns - trial keys
While entering a value:
- [bold]ENT[/bold] confirms the input - [bold]CLR[/bold] deletes the previous character - pressing [bold]CLR[/bold] on an empty field cancels the input
[bold]Frequencies[/bold] use the [bold]___.___[/bold] format.
Enter the megahertz digits first. Untouched digits are treated as zero. At least three digits must be entered.
[bold]Text[/bold] uses the letters assigned to each number key like a telephone keypad.
Press a key repeatedly to cycle through its letters.
[bold]0[/bold] enters a space, then a dash.
## Function switch
The rotary switch controls the radio's basic operating state.
- [bold]OFF[/bold] - switches the radio off - [bold]CT[/bold] - switches the radio on securely; selecting CT again cycles FH, SC, and CT - [bold]PT[/bold] - switches to unencrypted plain-text transmission - [bold]LD[/bold] - opens the fill page - [bold]Z[/bold] - arms ZEROIZE
[bold]LD[/bold] and [bold]Z[/bold] are sprung positions and return to the previous switch position after use.
They do not change the active waveform.
## Display readout
The top of the display remains visible across all faceplate pages.
It shows:
- [bold]RX / TX[/bold] - whether the radio is receiving or transmitting - [bold]SEC / UNSEC / CLEAR[/bold] - current encryption state - [bold]SIG[/bold] - working-net link quality - [bold]--DIR--[/bold] - shown instead of SIG when using a direct frequency - [bold]BAT[/bold] - remaining battery in four bars - current memory - frequency - net name - operating band - waveform - squelch - output power - active feature flags - [bold]STN[/bold] - transmitting callsign - [bold]BIT[/bold] - self-test status
Active feature flags can include:
- MON - SCAN - BURST - PS - PRI - EMCON - RXMT
[bold]BIT[/bold] normally shows [bold]PASS[/bold].
If the radio cannot operate normally, it displays the first detected problem, such as:
- NO CELL - OFF - STOWED - SRCH - NO NET
## PGM - net memory
PGM manages the radio's memories.
[bold]LOAD STD NETS[/bold] loads missing standard nets without replacing manually configured memories.
Each memory appears as a separate line.
A [bold]*[/bold] marks the current working memory.
Select a memory and press [bold]ENT[/bold] to open its options.
Available actions include:
- [bold]WORK THIS NET[/bold] - make the memory the working net - [bold]TUNE TO A NET[/bold] - select a known friendly net or resolved intercepted net - [bold]KEY A FREQUENCY[/bold] - enter a frequency manually - [bold]EMPTY THE MEMORY[/bold] - remove the memory's current contents - [bold]DELETE THE MEMORY[/bold] - remove the memory slot - [bold]RENAME[/bold] - change the memory label
[bold]ADD NET[/bold] creates another memory and prompts for a label.
### Direct frequencies
If a manually entered frequency matches a known net, that net is loaded normally.
Otherwise, it becomes a [bold]direct frequency[/bold].
Direct frequencies are:
- unrelayed - unencrypted - usable only by radios or tuned headsets on the same frequency
Valid direct frequencies must fall within:
- 1.000-2.999 MHz military band - 30.000+ MHz colony softwave band
## SEC - COMSEC
SEC manages encryption and fill cards.
It displays:
- [bold]SWITCH[/bold] - current function-switch position - [bold]FILL[/bold] - installed fill card - [bold]ISSUED TO[/bold] - faction associated with the fill - [bold]TRAFFIC[/bold] - whether transmissions are currently encrypted
Available actions include:
- [bold]ZEROIZE[/bold] - eject the fill card - [bold]DESTROY[/bold] - destroy the installed fill card - [bold]RECRYPTO[/bold] - replace your faction's current encryption key - [bold]SEND KEY OTA[/bold] - distribute the current key over the air
[bold]RECRYPTO[/bold] requires command authority.
ZEROIZE, DESTROY, RECRYPTO, and SEND KEY OTA require confirmation.
## SRCH - search receiver
The search receiver scans for hostile radio traffic.
[bold]START SEARCH[/bold] begins sweeping the band.
While searching, the radio:
- leaves all loaded nets - cannot transmit - consumes additional power
The SRCH page includes:
- [bold]HEAD[/bold] - current search frequency - [bold]CONTACTS[/bold] - detected signals - [bold]KEY ANALYSIS[/bold] - cryptographic analysis for factions with fixed nets - [bold]JAMMER DF[/bold] - jammer direction-finding tools
### Resolving contacts
Contacts become more precise as the radio observes additional transmissions.
A signal may appear as:
[bold]2XX.XXX[/bold]
then:
[bold]25X.XXX[/bold]
then:
[bold]259.XXX[/bold]
before resolving to its exact frequency and net.
Each new transmission contributes once toward identifying the contact.
A net transmitting approximately once per minute requires around three transmissions to resolve.
A busy net transmitting less than 20 seconds apart can resolve in roughly one minute.
Partial contacts retain their progress while transmissions continue.
Progress begins to decay after approximately two minutes without traffic.
### Search range
At MED output, transmitters can be detected within approximately 120 tiles.
HI increases this range by approximately 50%.
LO reduces the range to approximately 70 tiles.
Once a net is resolved, detectable transmissions on it can provide:
- a bearing toward the transmitter - approximate distance - a temporary tactical-map marker - one trial toward key analysis
Secured SC and CT transmissions do not provide bearings.
Select a [bold]resolved[/bold] contact and press ENT to tune it into the working memory.
Select a [bold]partial[/bold] contact and press ENT to begin [bold]Dwell[/bold].
## LOG
LOG displays recorded radio traffic.
[bold]NET FILTER[/bold] cycles between nets represented in the log.
[bold]INTERCEPTS ONLY[/bold] hides friendly traffic.
Available print functions are:
- [bold]PRINT LOG[/bold] - prints all recorded traffic - [bold]PRINT INTERCEPTS[/bold] - prints only intercepted traffic
Each traffic entry shows:
- time - sender - net - message
## OPT - configuration
OPT contains the radio's operating settings.
Press [bold]ENT[/bold] on most lines to cycle through available values.
### MODE
[bold]MODE[/bold] selects:
- FREQ HOP - SINGLE CH - CIPHER - PLAIN
See [textlink="the AN/PRC-117G" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] for waveform details.
### MONITOR and SCAN
[bold]MONITOR[/bold] and [bold]SCAN[/bold] provide the same functions available through the guided interface.
### SQUELCH
[bold]SQUELCH[/bold] ranges from 0 to 4.
Higher values suppress more static and degraded traffic.
Setting 4 can also suppress weak relay traffic.
The standard setting is 3.
### OUTPUT
[bold]OUTPUT[/bold] selects LO, MED, or HI power.
[bold]Power[/bold] [bold]Relay range[/bold] [bold]Battery use[/bold] [bold]DF chance[/bold]
LO 60% Half Half
MED 100% Standard Standard
HI 150% Double Double
### BACKLIGHT
[bold]BACKLIGHT[/bold] cycles between:
- night - day - off
### TECHNIQUES
[bold]TECHNIQUES[/bold] opens advanced operator functions:
- BURST TX - POWER SAVE - PRIORITY WATCH - EMCON - STAKED SET
These functions are explained below.
### STATION
[bold]STATION[/bold] controls the identity used by the radio and provides several utility functions.
- [bold]CALLSIGN[/bold] - assign a fixed station callsign of up to 16 characters - [bold]CLEAR OVERRIDE[/bold] - return to the current wearer's callsign - [bold]ROSTER[/bold] - select a standard station name - [bold]NET DIRECTORY[/bold] - open the communications directory - [bold]PHONE[/bold] - open the field telephone - [bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] - transmit a radio check
Fixed callsigns are useful for command posts and staked radios.
### SET STATUS
[bold]SET STATUS[/bold] displays:
- whether the radio is worn or staked - installed antenna - relayed nets - relay coverage - whether audio is using the headset or handset
### LINK
[bold]LINK[/bold] provides detailed connection information.
- [bold]QUALITY[/bold] - link quality percentage - [bold]VIA[/bold] - relay carrying the signal, including bearing and distance - [bold]DRAW[/bold] - current battery drain per second - [bold]ENDURANCE[/bold] - estimated remaining operating time
## Advanced operator functions
These functions are not required for normal radio operation.
They modify range, battery use, emissions, or radio behavior for specific situations.
### Burst transmission
[bold]OPT > TECHNIQUES > BURST TX[/bold]
Burst transmission compresses each message before sending it.
While enabled:
- transmission battery cost is reduced by 30% - direction-finding chance is reduced by 50% - message contents are unchanged
Burst can be combined with other radio settings.
### Power save
[bold]OPT > TECHNIQUES > POWER SAVE[/bold]
Power save allows the receiver to sleep between messages.
Idle battery consumption is reduced by 40%.
While active:
- SCAN is disabled - PRIORITY WATCH is disabled
Enabling SCAN or PRIORITY WATCH disables power save.
### Priority watch
[bold]OPT > TECHNIQUES > PRIORITY WATCH[/bold]
Priority watch monitors one additional loaded memory while keeping the current working memory unchanged.
Incoming traffic from the watched memory can be heard, but transmissions continue through the ON AIR memory.
Unlike SCAN, priority watch does not automatically change the working memory.
### EMCON
[bold]OPT > TECHNIQUES > EMCON[/bold]
EMCON places the radio into a receive-only emissions-control state.
While active, the radio performs no:
- transmissions - relay traffic - telephone traffic
Because the radio does not transmit, it produces no direction-finding signature.
The radio continues to:
- receive traffic on its working net - record received traffic
Idle battery draw is reduced to one quarter of normal.
[bold]An AN/PRC in EMCON provides no relay coverage.[/bold]
Headsets relying on that radio for relay access will lose their combat nets.
### Retransmission bridge
[bold]OPT > TECHNIQUES > STAKED SET[/bold]
This function is available while the radio is staked down.
Select:
- [bold]SIDE A[/bold] - [bold]SIDE B[/bold]
Each side must contain a named net loaded into one of the radio's memories.
Select [bold]BRIDGE[/bold] to connect them.
Traffic received on either net is retransmitted onto the other.
Retransmitted messages preserve the original speaker and are marked [bold][RXMT][/bold].
For example:
[bold][RXMT] SABRE 1-1: contact north[/bold]
Retransmissions:
- consume battery - can produce a direction-finding signature - cannot be retransmitted again
This prevents bridged radios from creating retransmission loops.
Packing up the radio immediately ends the bridge.
### Peak the antenna
[bold]OPT > TECHNIQUES > STAKED SET > PEAK THE ANTENNA[/bold]
Peaking the antenna takes approximately 15 seconds.
The radio must remain stationary while the antenna is tuned.
Once complete, relay range increases by 25%.
The bonus remains until the radio is packed up.
### Over-the-air rekey
[bold]SEC > SEND KEY OTA[/bold]
After a recrypto, radios containing old fill cards have an outdated key.
An operator with the current key can distribute it over the air.
The display shows how many outdated friendly radios are currently reachable.
Press [bold]ENT[/bold] once to arm the transmission, then again to send it.
The new key reaches friendly radios that are:
- switched on - worn or staked - within approximately 45 tiles
Radios can also receive the key at greater distances if both sets are connected through the faction's command-net relay network.
Sending a key:
- consumes a large amount of battery - can produce a direction-finding signature - has a 30-second cooldown
[bold]Captured radios containing one of your faction's fill cards are still treated as friendly sets.[/bold]
If one is reachable, it also receives the new key.
Invalidate compromised keys before distributing a replacement whenever possible.
### Dwell
Dwell operates while the search receiver is active.
On the [bold]SRCH[/bold] page, select a partial contact and press [bold]ENT[/bold].
The search head stops sweeping and remains on that contact.
While dwelling:
- each new transmission counts twice toward resolving the contact - all other frequencies are ignored
Select [bold]RELEASE THE HEAD[/bold] to resume normal searching.
The search automatically resumes when the contact fully resolves.
### Key analysis
Key analysis can recover the encryption key of a resolved hostile faction net.
Enemy keys contain six different symbols from [bold]A[/bold] through [bold]H[/bold].
Each encrypted transmission received from a resolved enemy net provides one [bold]trial[/bold].
A radio can store up to 12 trials.
To test a key:
- open [bold]SRCH > KEY ANALYSIS[/bold] - select the enemy faction - select [bold]TEST A TRIAL KEY[/bold] - enter six letters
Letters use the keypad's text-entry system.
After testing, the radio reports how many symbols are in the correct position.
For example:
[bold]2/6[/bold]
The radio does not identify which symbols are correct.
Trial results remain available and can be compared when testing later combinations.
At [bold]6/6[/bold], the key is broken.
That radio can then read the faction's encrypted traffic:
- live - in its radio log
A broken key does [bold]not[/bold]:
- allow transmission on enemy nets - transfer to another radio
A recrypto removes:
- the broken key - stored trials - previous trial results
Key-analysis progress belongs to the radio itself and remains with the set if it is captured.
Key analysis requires a trained operator.
### Jammer direction finding
The search receiver can locate an active jammer.
While affected by a jammer, open:
[bold]SRCH > JAMMER DF[/bold]
To establish a fix:
- select [bold]TAKE A BEARING[/bold] - move at least 12 tiles - check [bold]BASELINE[/bold] to confirm sufficient movement - select [bold]TAKE SECOND BEARING[/bold]
The radio compares both bearings and places the estimated jammer position on your faction's tactical map.
The marker remains for approximately two minutes.
The radio also reports the jammer's distance.
The first bearing expires after three minutes.
## Returning to automatic settings
Settings changed from the faceplate remain active when returning to the guided interface.
The guided panel displays any manually changed settings.
Select [bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold] to restore the guided panel's normal configuration.
This resets manually configured operating settings back to their automatic values.
## Practice drill
The following drill demonstrates the main faceplate controls on a powered, worn radio with no nets loaded.
- Press [bold]8[/bold] to open PGM. - Select [bold]LOAD STD NETS[/bold] and press ENT. - Press [bold]7[/bold] to open OPT. - Set [bold]OUTPUT[/bold] to LO. - Enable [bold]BURST TX[/bold]. - Enable [bold]PRIORITY WATCH[/bold] and select the command memory. - Press [bold]1[/bold] to send a radio check. - Open [bold]LINK[/bold] and check the current relay and estimated endurance. - Return to the guided interface. - Open SETTINGS and confirm that the manual settings are shown. - Press [bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold].
The [bold]?[/bold] soft key opens the faceplate key card at any time.
